title: Microsoft Purview: view-only role management for Global Reader and Security Reader
summary: Hold: the risk rationale says nobody's permissions change, although the briefing correctly describes new permission to view member assignments. The roadmap facts and documented controls are supported; the licensing context, Graph property names and Purview navigation headings also need small corrections.

claims.quote: Searched: '"Purview" "view-only role management" enable disable settings'; read purview/purview-permissions, defender-office-365/scc-permissions and Entra manage-roles-portal. These document existing assignment controls, not a separate switch for the new role.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: risk; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Global Reader can read settings and administrative information across Microsoft 365 but cannot take management actions.
claims.quote: Users in this role can read settings and administrative information across Microsoft 365 services but can't take management actions. Global Reader is the read-only counterpart to Global Administrator.

claims.where: Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Security Reader members have read-only access to many security features.
claims.quote: Members have read-only access to many security features of Identity Protection Center, Privileged Identity Management, Monitor Microsoft 365 Service Health, and the Defender and compliance portals.

claims.where: Scope; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: The Global Reader Entra role maps to the Purview Global Reader role group.
claims.quote: | Entra role | Description | Mapped Purview role groups | ... | **Global Reader** | The read-only version of the **Global administrator** role. View all settings and administrative information across Microsoft 365. ... | Global Reader |

claims.where: Scope; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: The Security Reader Entra role maps to the Purview Security Reader role group.
claims.quote: the Security Reader role from Microsoft Entra ID is assigned to this role group. Therefore, this role group inherits the capabilities and membership of the Security Reader role from Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: When an account has both an Entra role and a scoped Purview role group assignment, the Entra role takes precedence and effective permissions are unscoped.
claims.quote: the Entra role takes precedence at runtime. As a result, the user's effective permissions are unscoped, even if a scoped Microsoft Purview role group assignment also exists.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The two cited Purview permissions pages do not yet list the new view-only role management role or document its separately named portal appearance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview view-only role management 566529 Global Reader Security Reader enable disable default licensing requirements'; read purview/purview-permissions and searched scc-permissions for Global Reader, Security Reader and View-Only Role. No new role name appears.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity and Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The new role is described as view-only, with no stated assignment-changing or autonomous action capability.
claims.quote: a new view-only role management role to give admins permissions to see all the member assignments in Purview and Defender portal.

claims.where: rationale: risk; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The risk rationale says the change is not a change to anyone's permissions, although the body says the new role grants permission to see assignments and extends what the reader roles can see.
claims.quote: the exposure is wider visibility of who holds which role, not a change to anyone's permissions. ... Adding a role that lists role group members extends what those two roles can see, without changing what they can change.
claims.fix: In the risk rationale, replace 'not a change to anyone's permissions' with 'not a grant of permission to change assignments'. The change adds read permission; it is not documented as adding write permission.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The action rating is prepare even though the briefing says the default is unknown and no source says existing behaviour changes for administrators who do not act.
claims.quote: action: "prepare" ... Microsoft has not stated whether tenants must do anything for the role to take effect, so no source says existing behaviour changes for administrators who do not act.
claims.fix: Set action to 'review'. The assessment scale places a new capability with unknown default and no stated change to existing behaviour in review; retain the advice to assess reader-role membership.
